subject: candidate_generation_is_lossy_upstream_of_uncertainty
prediction: the framework's errors are mostly bad choices among candidates the uncertainty machinery can see and hedge

A bad choice among VISIBLE candidates is hedged (inferred/contingent/low-confidence) and was how VC-0002/VC-0005 were caught; a LOST candidate is silent. Candidate generation has now failed in BOTH directions — over-generation (bros, VC-0012) and loss (nubile, VC-0020) — while role/fragility errors sit on the visible-candidate side. It is the layer where the structural corrections cluster.
evidence: 5-site candidate-loss audit: 9 discards, 8 genuine scaffolding, 1 real loss (nubile slug, echoed in filename + matches title). The corroboration discriminator (filename echo, title match) fired on the one lost candidate and on 0 scaffolding across all 5 sites (0/9 false positives).

notes: FAILURE TAXONOMY established (5 classes): candidate_loss, candidate_over_generation, bad_candidate_selection, capability_boundary, insufficient_evidence. The durable lesson: a loss DEFEATS the safeguards; a bad selection TRIPS them. Loss is qualitatively worse than a choice error of equal frequency. This is the second candidate-generation finding (bros was the first); the layer, not the role rules, is the architectural locus.
